**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part**: Compound leaf (tomato)
- **Key features**:
  - Numerous small to medium (2-5mm), dark brown, roughly circular spots scattered uniformly across the leaf surface
  - Some spots show lighter tan/gray centers with darker brown margins
  - Some necrotic centers appear to have fallen out (shot-hole effect)
  - Leaf remains mostly green; no large concentric-ring lesions, no white powdery coating, no yellow mosaic pattern

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Classic presentation is small circular spots with dark borders and lighter centers on tomato leaves, scattered uniformly — matches very well
- **Early Blight**: Would show larger lesions with concentric rings (target spot) — not evident here
- **Bacterial Speck**: Spots would be very tiny (<2mm) with yellow halos — spots here are larger and no clear halos
- **Leaf Mold**: Yellowing with olive mold on underside — not seen
- **Powdery Mildew**: White coating — absent

The numerous small, uniformly scattered circular lesions with dark borders and lighter centers on a tomato compound leaf are hallmark symptoms of Septoria leaf spot.
